segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn. I'm Georgie.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. To watch a video version of this podcast and download a free worksheet, go to our website bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hi Neil, how are you? Are you happy to be at work today?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Of course, I'm always happy to be at work.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Great. Well, today we are talking about dream jobs.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Obviously, this job is amazing, but we're going to talk about some different jobs we'd like to do.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Sounds good. Shall we start?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Georgie, when you were a child, what did you want to do when you grew up?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What was your dream job?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, when I was really little, about five or six, I remember telling people that I wanted to be a princess.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: when I realized that wasn't going to be possible for me.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: My next dream was to be a pop star

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: because my friends and I used to write songs

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: and perform in front of our parents and I thought that would be really fun Yeah what about you

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well kind of similar

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think actually when I was a child,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I thought that being a professional sportsman would be fantastic,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: either a footballer or a cricketer.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What went wrong?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm not good enough.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I learned that lesson.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But also I wanted, when I got a little bit older, sort of teenage, and started playing guitar, I thought, yeah, maybe a rock star would be the thing for me.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So Neil, obviously you are not a rock star, but how or when did you decide to become an English teacher instead?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, when I finished university, I wanted to travel more than anything else.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I wanted to live in foreign countries, not just go on holiday.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I thought a good way to do that would be to become an English teacher.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, I have a similar story. It was the same thing for me. I just wanted to live abroad.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Georgie, what is important to you about your job now?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well many of us spend a lot of our lives working so for me it really important to enjoy the day We work nine to five it a lot of hours in the day It really important to me to have a nice team that you can have fun with

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It's also really important for me to feel like I'm giving something good or doing a good job.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I think it's important to feel that you're doing something useful. So hopefully, our conversations like this are useful for people, because they can learn something. And I like that.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, me too. So Neil, if you didn't have to worry about money or anything else, what would your dream job be? I think I know the answer already.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, well, you said earlier that I didn't become a rock star, but there is still a future. And, you know, if I didn't have to work, I could just follow my dream. How about you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think if I didn't do this job, I would like to be a travel photographer or someone

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: that makes documentaries I really love those nature documentaries and it would be very fun to be involved in those

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes that sounds like it would be amazing

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, let's recap the language we heard during the conversation. We can describe something

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: like a job as important to us. For example, I said that a nice team at work is important to me.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We talked about our dream jobs when we were children, using the structure, when I was younger, I wanted to be.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, for example, when I was younger, I wanted to be a footballer.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And we talked about our dream jobs now using conditionals.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, for example, if I could do any job, I would be a travel photographer.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And when we're talking about jobs, we can do them or we can be them.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, I teach English or I am an English teacher.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And that's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you like our programmes, why not sign up to our email newsletter?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: You can get suggestions for other English lessons you might enjoy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: There's a link in the notes for this programme.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Next time, we'll talk about lunch.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Join us again.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Bye.
